doc.title: Al Gafa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 2, 2023

title: His daughters' view of his profession
summary: His daughters love jazz; his youngest studied singing and he performed with her.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Talking about my children and grandchildren

blocks.x: Glad to hear that. And what did your kids — you have one kid? One child?
Do you — what did they think of your profession?

Now they absolutely love it you know. And they were always aware that I was a guitar player. My youngest daughter had wanted to become a singer. She was a fairly decent singer. And I didn’t have the — I didn’t want to discourage her because this is a tough business. I’m not kidding, this is a really disgusting business sometimes. And for female singers in it it’s even worse because they’re — everybody promises them everything but they don’t come through. And so I didn’t have the — I didn’t want to discourage her from becoming one and she went a year and a half to Purchase college and studied music and then the college was just too much off the New York scene for her. She loved the New York scene, she loved the cabaret scene in New York. She loved the club scene, not the cabaret scene. She loved the club scene in New York and Purchase, New York is — you know the lights go out at 8:30 I think over there. So that was not for her. She did not stay. But she came back home, I lived pretty close to a college and she enrolled in the music program at the college. And I volunteered to stop in and I did a performance with her that was absolutely — she sung “When I Fall in Love,” just guitar and voice. I had tears in my eyes, I’m on the stand with just my daughter. It was beautiful. So that’s a crowning part in my life. I can not replace that. That was beautiful. And my other daughter, when she got married they invited us over for dinner and she’s playing all these jazz things in the background, you know, on YouTube or something. And I said, “Gee I didn’t know that you liked this kind of music.” She said, “Well I’ve been around it all my life and it’s part of my life.” All right. Yeah. And still today when my wife and I go there for dinner there’s jazz in the background. My youngest daughter likes hip hop every once in a while but that doesn’t usually last for long. Either somebody gets mad or I get mad you know, and then we take it off.
You’re making my face hurt, Al, from smiling so much. I’ve had some similar experiences and you can’t beat it.
